Our extended family reunion happens once every few years, pulling together relatives from all over, a lot of whom I only really know from old photos and vague childhood memories, faces I can barely match to actual names anymore.
Apparently, over the years, I'd started looking a lot like my cousin on my mom's side.
I hadn't actually seen her in person since we were both kids running around at the last reunion.
The first relative who greeted me at the door hugged me immediately, calling me by my cousin's name.
She asked enthusiastically about a job I'd never had in a city I'd never actually lived in.
I stood there for a second, genuinely unsure whether to correct her right away or just play along, mostly out of sheer confusion at that point.
I corrected her gently, and she laughed it off, blaming the resemblance.
But within the hour, at least four more relatives made the exact same mistake, each one apologizing the same nervous, embarrassed way every single time.
By the second mix-up, I honestly stopped correcting people right away, mostly out of curiosity.
I just wanted to see how long an entire conversation could go before someone eventually realized I wasn't who they thought.
One uncle spent a genuinely impressive fifteen minutes discussing my cousin's supposed new apartment renovation with me.
He nodded along enthusiastically to updates about a bathroom remodel I knew absolutely nothing about.
I nodded along too, occasionally throwing in a vague "yeah, it's coming along" whenever he paused for a response.
Apparently that was convincing enough, and he never once suspected anything was off.
My actual cousin showed up a little later, and the two of us stood next to each other.
Relatives kept glancing back and forth, visibly recalculating every conversation they'd already had with either of us that day.
Several people visibly turned slightly pink with embarrassment.
We ended up leaning into it for the rest of the weekend, answering to each other's names occasionally just to mess with people.
Honestly, it became the funniest running joke of the entire reunion, and a few relatives even started just calling us both "the cousins" collectively.
Now there's a family group chat meme about "the great cousin mix-up." At the next reunion, someone's already threatening to make us wear name tags, just so relatives can finally keep us straight.

My cousin actually suggested matching t-shirts instead, with our names printed in giant letters across the front, which honestly sounds embarrassing enough that half the family is already looking forward to it.
